caption: The image is a technical drawing rendered in pencil on a beige background, showing three orthographic views of an oak chest. The top left section displays a front elevation, annotated with a width of 4 feet (4'0") and a height of 1 foot 8 inches (1'8"). The bottom left section presents a detailed front view; it features three rectangular panels with symmetrical, linear geometric designs and a decorative apron at the bottom, containing measurements such as 2 feet 3 5/8 inches tall and various component widths. The chest is mounted on short legs with ornamental curved cutouts. The right section depicts a side elevation, specifying features like the depth of the chest (1 foot 6 inches), panel dimensions, and hinge placement. In the top right, there are handwritten notes: "OAK CHEST (1697)," "BROOKLYN MUSEUM," and "SCALE ⅛"=1'," as well as the name "Robert Brigadier" and the date "1/26/56." Additional notations describe construction details such as "COVER HINGES ON WOODEN PEG." All lines and text are in monochrome pencil, and the layout is clean with precise dimension annotations.
